questions.question: What does population size describe?
choices: The total land area alone
The average age alone
The number of individuals in a defined population
The amount of rainfall alone

questions.question: What does per-capita resource use mean?
choices: Resource use per continent regardless of population
The total amount of resource left underground
The maximum amount any one factory can use
Resource use per person

questions.question: Which change adds people to a region's population without a birth?
choices: Immigration
Emigration
Mortality
A decline in birth rate

questions.question: What is carrying capacity in a resource-limited context?
choices: A permanent number unaffected by resources
The population a system can support under stated conditions
The number of people ever born
The number of buildings alone

questions.question: What is resource depletion?
choices: Permanent creation of unlimited new resources
The movement of clouds over a city
Reduction of a resource stock when use exceeds replacement
A change only in product labels

questions.question: What does a water footprint estimate?
choices: Only the water stored in one drinking bottle
Only the number of rivers in a country
Only the rainfall reaching a building's roof
Direct and indirect water use associated with a person, product, or activity

questions.question: What does an age-structure diagram show?
choices: Numbers or proportions of people in different age groups
The exact future population without assumptions
Only the area's temperature
The locations of every workplace

questions.question: Why does population size alone not determine total resource use?
choices: Every resident has identical consumption needs and habits
Per-person use also differs among populations
Population size alone fixes all resource use
Land area alone fixes consumption regardless of people

questions.question: How can technology change resource demand?
choices: It always reduces every impact regardless of how it is used
It leaves every material requirement unchanged
It can change efficiency and which materials are required
It prevents consumption from rising with expanded activity

questions.question: Why can carrying capacity change over time?
choices: It is defined by one fixed global number
People never alter resource systems
Only births can affect resources
Resources, technology, and environmental conditions can change

questions.question: Why can improved efficiency fail to reduce total consumption as much as expected?
choices: Expanded use can offset some savings
Per-use savings always guarantee the same total reduction
Efficient devices cannot be operated more often
Efficiency changes resource supply but never demand

questions.question: How can dense development reduce some per-person infrastructure needs?
choices: Density necessarily eliminates all environmental impacts
Shared services and shorter travel can lower certain inputs
All travel and water use become zero
Sharing infrastructure always raises per-person material use

questions.question: Why are population projections usually reported with assumptions?
choices: Birth and death rates are permanently fixed everywhere
A projection gives an exact count regardless of migration
Future births, deaths, and migration are uncertain
Assumptions guarantee that only one outcome is possible

questions.question: Why can equal total water use hide different pressures on supply?
choices: Water is replenished at identical rates in all places
Equal use always means equal scarcity
Water availability depends only on population size
Local water availability and replenishment can differ

questions.question: How does renewable-resource stock differ from its replacement rate?
choices: Stock is an amount available; rate is replenishment per unit time
Both are amounts stored at one moment
The rate is the total amount currently available
The stock is the amount entering per unit time

questions.question: A town has 1,000 people using 100 L each per day. What is total daily use?
One town has twice as many residents but half the per-person energy use of another. How do their total uses compare?
choices: The larger town uses twice as much
The larger town uses half as much
They are equal
The larger town uses four times as much

questions.question: A population starts at 10,000, with 200 births, 100 deaths, 50 immigrants, and 150 emigrants in a year. What is its final size?
A reservoir receives 80 units of water per day while 100 units are withdrawn, with other flows negligible. What is the daily storage change?
choices: A decrease of 20 units
An increase of 20 units
A decrease of 180 units
No change

questions.question: A report predicts future resource use from constant per-person consumption. What important follow-up should be considered?
choices: Assume per-person consumption can never change
Whether per-person consumption may change
Use population totals without considering any consumption rate
Treat all future resources as unlimited
